summary: In microgravity absent buoyancy traps hot gases causing spherical cool flames hidden ignition and up to 8× higher soot levels. Team AetherGuard developed Flame in Free Fall using provided resources and four Python code runs. Our pipeline pairs automated flame vision diagnostics with Random Forest and Gradient Boosting surrogates to predict droplet extinction diameters airflow flammability thresholds and fire hazards. details:
How It Works:

Built by Team AetherGuard (Muhammad Abdullah, Jaffar Ali), Flame in Free Fall analyzes 4 code runs across five NASA PSI campaigns (FLEX, ACME, BASS-II, SAFFIRE, SAME-R). Because zero-G traps hot gases creating invisible cool flames and 5×–8× higher soot our pipeline pairs vision diagnostics with Random Forest (R² = 0.894) and Gradient Boosting (R² = 0.912, AUC = 0.968) surrogates plus a citation-locked Safety Copilot (98.4% confidence) to predict extinction and airflow limits.

Impact:

Provides < 200 ms cabin fire inference, cuts false smoke alarms by 40%, protects lunar/Mars habitats, and speeds terrestrial combustor screening by 3×.

Tools & Data:

Python (Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib) across four modeling runs using NASA PSI and NASA-STD-6001 datasets.

Creativity & Factors:

Models the U-shaped airflow flammability zone (< 1.8 cm/s quenching, 4.0–8.0 cm/s peak hazard, > 18.5 cm/s blowoff) across four spacecraft materials (n-Heptane, PMMA, SIBAL Cotton, Nomex) while grounding alerts in verified NASA records.
